items.label: f01-storage-hydration
items.front: crmpyjs auth.store rehydrates the session with a direct cast from parsed JSON. Risk, test and fix?
items.back: Malformed or wrong-shape storage causes boot/runtime bugs. Test: malformed storage hydration. Fix: validate the storage payload with a schema; the critique also suggests storing only the refresh token and deriving the user via /me.

items.label: f02-hardcoded-base-url
items.front: The frontend client.ts holds a literal API base URL on line 1. Impact and fix?
items.back: It breaks when the app runs on another host or environment. Move it to Vite env config (fallback only for local dev) and test both dev and production builds before merging.

items.label: f03-what-seniors-check
items.front: Three auth questions a senior asks of this CRM backend?
items.back: Is every sensitive route protected at the server layer? Are role names the only auth source, or are there resource ownership checks too? Do persisted refresh tokens have lifecycle parity with the JWT expiry config?

items.prompt: RequireAuth redirects logged-out users to /login. What does it protect?

choices.text: Both UI and API, because it validates the token's signature
The session blob, because it validates local storage with a schema
The API data, because protected routes never load without a session
The UI alone, because direct backend calls skip the redirect

The session blob, because it validates local storage with a schema
The API data, because protected routes never load without a session
The UI alone, because direct backend calls skip the redirect

items.explanation: 'Validation and authorization: None on the client. This is UX gating only.' and 'A user can still call backend endpoints directly unless the server also checks auth.'

choices.text: The raw Response object, so the caller can read the JSON
A plain Error with just the message, because the code is dropped
undefined, because non-OK responses resolve like 204s
A typed ApiError carrying status 401 and the code INVALID_CREDENTIALS

A plain Error with just the message, because the code is dropped
undefined, because non-OK responses resolve like 204s

items.explanation: apiRequest does `throw new Error(errorBody?.message ?? 'Request failed')`; the trace notes it 'loses structured error codes', weakening typed UI handling.

items.prompt: The seed script throws halfway through inserting opportunities. What state is the dev database left in?

choices.text: Partially seeded, since no outer transaction wraps the writes
Unchanged, because Prisma rolls back the whole script on error
Empty, because the script deletes everything again on failure
Fully seeded, because Prisma retries failed creates automatically

choices: Partially seeded, since no outer transaction wraps the writes
Unchanged, because Prisma rolls back the whole script on error
Empty, because the script deletes everything again on failure

items.explanation: 'There is no transaction wrapping the whole seed, so partial state is possible on failure.' The register suggests intentionally failing mid-seed as the test.

items.prompt: authMiddleware verifies a JWT successfully. What does that verification NOT establish?

choices.text: That the token was signed with the server's own secret key
That the user may still access the specific resource requested
That req.user can be hydrated with the id, email and role
That the token has not yet passed its expiry time

choices: That the token was signed with the server's own secret key
That the user may still access the specific resource requested
That req.user can be hydrated with the id, email and role
That the token has not yet passed its expiry time

items.explanation: 'JWT verification proves token validity, not that the user still has permission for every resource shape.'

items.prompt: Someone dumps the RefreshToken table. What do they get for each row's token?

choices.text: The access token, since refresh tokens are never persisted
A hash of each refresh token rather than the raw token
The user's bcrypt password hash, used to re-sign tokens
The raw signed refresh JWT, ready to replay

choices: The access token, since refresh tokens are never persisted
A hash of each refresh token rather than the raw token
The user's bcrypt password hash, used to re-sign tokens
The raw signed refresh JWT, ready to replay

items.explanation: Login stores `tokenHash: hashToken(refreshToken)`; 'The refresh token is persisted hashed, not raw.' Each row also keeps its id, user and expiry.

None yet: RBAC is defined but no feature route uses requirePermission

choices.text: They still expire after 7 days, since the DB expiry is hard-coded in the service
Login fails at startup, because the two expiry settings must match
They never expire, because only the JWT itself carries an expiry
They expire after 1 day, because expiresAt is read from the env file

items.explanation: auth.service.ts writes `expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)`; the risk register calls this refresh-token expiry drift and suggests deriving it from config.

items.prompt: The /me controller reads req.user!.id. What makes that non-null assertion safe?

choices.text: Zod validation: req.user is checked before every controller runs
The route order alone: authMiddleware runs before the controller
The Express runtime: it always populates req.user from the Authorization header
The declaration merge: express.d.ts guarantees req.user at runtime

choices: Zod validation: req.user is checked before every controller runs

items.explanation: req.user exists only via declaration merging (types) plus the middleware (runtime); 'req.user! is safe only because route registration order is correct.' TypeScript does not check that order.

items.prompt: What startup invariant does server.ts maintain by awaiting prisma.$connect() before app.listen?

choices.text: The app listens first so health checks pass while Prisma connects
No listener is bound until config and Prisma are both ready
Prisma reconnects automatically, so listen order does not matter
Env parsing is deferred until the first request arrives at a route

No listener is bound until config and Prisma are both ready
Prisma reconnects automatically, so listen order does not matter
Env parsing is deferred until the first request arrives at a route

items.explanation: 'The invariant is "no listener until config and Prisma are ready."' Env is parsed eagerly at import time, so a missing variable crashes startup early.

items.prompt: The database is down but the API process is running. What do GET /health and GET /health/db return?

choices.text: /health fails and /health/db returns database: disconnected
Both fail, because /health checks the Prisma connection first
Both return ok, because Prisma connected successfully at startup
/health stays ok, while /health/db fails because its SELECT 1 errors

choices: /health fails and /health/db returns database: disconnected
Both fail, because /health checks the Prisma connection first
Both return ok, because Prisma connected successfully at startup
/health stays ok, while /health/db fails because its SELECT 1 errors

items.explanation: /health returns a static JSON status and never touches the DB ('can succeed even if DB is down'); /health/db runs prisma.$queryRaw`SELECT 1` and passes errors to next().
